text: Today, we’re introducing spaces, an interactive way to build a more personalized Muse. A space is a custom experience you create inside Muse by describing your idea, like a holiday gift tracker, a daily word game, or a planning board for your next DIY project. It’s shaped around your routines, goals, and interests, and can be as practical or entertaining as you want. Every space you create becomes part of Muse, so you can keep it where you want and come back to it any time. Have an idea you’ve been meaning to try? Tell Muse about it, and it builds it for you. Your initial idea is just the starting point. As you use your space, you can keep adjusting it with Muse, whether that’s adding what’s missing, trying a new look, or changing how it works. You can also choose where your spaces live in Muse. Add them to your sidebar, move them into your main tabs, hide the ones you don’t need right now, and schedule when they appear. For example, keep your weekly planner up front during the workweek, then swap it for your weekend plans on Saturday. Spaces can help you get things done, have a little fun, or give your creative projects a home. Here are a few ideas: Got a half-finished idea sitting in your notes app, a spreadsheet you keep meaning to clean up, or a hobby you want to dive into? Chances are you can turn it into a space. Your spaces are personal from the start. Connect the apps you use, and your spaces keep themselves up to date in the background, so new concert dates, price changes, or savings progress show up without you having to ask. You can check things off, add notes, and make edits right in your space, and everything will be there when you return. Starting today, spaces are available everywhere Muse is available. We’re also exploring ways for you to share your spaces with others to build a more collaborative experience in Muse. We’re also rolling out specialized versions of our models to Muse, trained with learnings from Muse Wonder, to make your overall experience even better.
